tools.name: check_token
tools.description:
Check if a crypto token is a scam before buying. `text` can be a contract address, a DexScreener or
    pump.fun link, or a whole forwarded "gem" message, on any of 64 networks (chain "auto" detects it; or pass a
    DexScreener chain id like "ton", "sui", "tron", "hyperevm"). Returns a rule-based v

tools.name: scan_message
tools.description:
Scan a crypto pitch message for scam tactics (seed phrase requests, wallet-drainer links,
    guaranteed returns, urgency, send-to-receive) without touching the network. Private data is stripped.

tools.name: token_history
tools.description: What RugRadar saw the last time this token was checked (verdict, score, pool size, how long ago).

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.description: Plain-language meaning of a RugRadar finding code such as HONEYPOT or LP_UNLOCKED.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description:
Fetch a saved RugRadar check by its id (the code at the end of a rugradar-dun.vercel.app/r/... link).
    Saved checks last 30 days. Re-run check_token before relying on an old one: tokens change fast.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_token, scan_message · Private data: check_token, scan_message, token_history, get_report · Public sink: scan_message · Destructive: get_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_token, scan_message · Private data: check_token, scan_message, token_history, get_report · Public sink: scan_message · Destructive: get_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
